reviewFindings.summary: raiseNeedsYou generated an id as sha256({question, taskId, at}) with no uniqueness guard; two identical questions raised in the same clock tick (guaranteed under a fixed/mocked clock) would collide, permanently stranding the older entry as unresolvable and locking the run in NEEDS_YOU forever.
reviewFindings.fix: Added an insertion-ordinal (next.needsYou.length) to the hash input in tsf/domain/keep-going.mjs. Regression test added in keep-going.test.mjs proving two identical-content questions get distinct ids and both resolve cleanly.

reviewFindings.summary: startKeepGoingRun/pauseKeepGoingRun/resumeKeepGoingRun did read-modify-write on persisted operator state with no optimistic-concurrency check, even though the run already carries a revision field and the codebase has an established assertExpectedRevision pattern (mission-state.mjs, adoption.mjs) for exactly this. Two concurrent requests for the same project could silently lose a transition.
reviewFindings.fix: Added expectedRevision support to keep-going.mjs's transitionRun (and thus pauseRun/resumeRun), matching mission-state.mjs's transitionMission pattern exactly (assertExpectedRevision from canonical.mjs, optional param, backward compatible). Threaded expectedRevision through keep-going-controller.mjs, keep-going-http-routes.mjs (now returns 409 TSF_STALE_REVISION on conflict, not 422), api.ts, and KeepGoingPanel.tsx (sends run.revision on every pause/resume). Domain-level, controller-level, and HTTP-level regression tests added; browser-confirmed the happy path still works transparently.

reviewFindings.summary: StartForm never collected a budget value even though this program's own wave-6 state.json entry claimed the UI closes the acceptance criterion 'literally (goal/Usage Mode/budget/constraints/stop conditions... all present and real)' -- an overclaim in the program's own durable record, not just a missing feature.

Browser-confirmed the defaults render and a started run carries them.

reviewFindings.summary: mapOrchestrationFacts always emits lastHeartbeatAt: null (no real timestamp exists in worker-list output today, by design -- see wave 3), so detectStall (Date.parse(null) => NaN) can never flag a real worker as stalled once this projection is wired into a live run.
reviewFindings.fix: No code change -- there is no real timestamp source to use without fabricating one, which the program discipline explicitly forbids. Already documented as a known limitation in the wave-3/wave-4 code comments and state.json entries; strengthened nothing further tonight but leaving this exact limitation as a recorded, open gap rather than silently accepting it as resolved.
